section.title: Scope
section.para: This chapter covers SAT structures, DIMACS ingestion, and deterministic parser failures. The parser must reject malformed inputs early and preserve clear semantics for callers. Examples here map directly to sattyre::SATProblem and parse_dimacs_file behavior.

section.title: DIMACS fundamentals
section.para: Comment lines begin with c and can appear before the problem line. The problem line defines variable and clause declarations and should be validated. Each clause must terminate with literal 0.

literallayout.computeroutput: c tiny satisfiable sample p cnf 3 2 1 -2 0 2 3 0

section.title: Validation expectations
section.para: Out-of-range literal ids must fail when absolute literal exceeds declared variable count. Clause lines without terminating zero must fail. Mismatch between declared and parsed clause counts should fail clearly.

section.title: Edge semantics
section.para: An empty formula with zero clauses is SAT by convention but still parsed as a valid problem. An empty clause denotes UNSAT structure and should be preserved as an empty clause entry. Literal sign encodes polarity; absolute value encodes variable index.

section.title: Test design
section.para: Write tests for normal, malformed, and boundary cases. Use small CNF files so failures are obvious and reproducible. Check exact exceptions or statuses to prevent silent behavior drift.

literallayout.computeroutput: cmake -S . -B build/sat-tests -DSATTYRE_ENABLE_TESTS=ON cmake --build build/sat-tests -j ctest --test-dir build/sat-tests -R sattyre-sat-parser-test --output-on-failure

section.title: Chapter summary
section.para: SAT correctness begins with a strict parser, not with advanced solver heuristics. If parser behavior is unstable, downstream solver and CLI behavior cannot be trusted. Treat parse errors as first-class API outcomes.

literallayout.computeroutput: // Good parser output should be deterministic for a given input. // Keep regression coverage close to edge-case inputs.
